authorities.holding: A spouse of a marriage declared void under HMA s.11 is entitled to SEEK permanent alimony under HMA s.25 ('any decree' in s.25 includes a decree declaring a marriage void) and interim maintenance under HMA s.24 during s.11 proceedings. Grant is discretionary and depends on the facts of each case and the conduct of the parties.
limits: Entitlement to seek, not entitlement to receive: relief is discretionary.

Does NOT remove the decree requirement for s.25: s.25 still operates 'at the time of passing any decree or at any time subsequent thereto'. Gives NO support to 'HMA 25 with no decree' fires — those remain forbidden.
Reference answered on law only; the matters were remitted to an appropriate Bench for decision on the merits. The eventual merits outcome is irrelevant to Laya's use.
Distinguishes CrPC s.125 / HAMA s.18 authorities (Yamunabai Adhav, Savitaben Bhatiya) as different remedial fields — do not extend the holding there.

authorities.case: Balkrishna Ramchandra Kadam v. Sangeeta Balkrishna Kadam
authorities.claimed_proposition: HMA s.27 is ancillary: the Matrimonial Court may make provision in the decree for property presented 'at or about the time of marriage' belonging jointly to husband and wife; recovery is 'by including it in the decree in the matrimonial proceedings'. Also reads 'at or about the time of marriage' broadly (property need not be given only at the wedding itself).

authorities.claimed_proposition: HMA s.27 is ancillary: there must be a matrimonial proceeding pending under the Act and the s.27 application must be made before that proceeding is decided (para 18, principle (ii)); exclusive Stridhan (property given separately to one spouse) is outside s.27 (paras 20-21); a freestanding Stridhan claim is maintainable instead as a CPC s.151 application before the Family Court under Family Courts Act s.7(1) Expl. (c) (paras 25-29); Devika Joshi overruled in part.
authorities.verification_required: Read the full primary judgment (SCC OnLine Chh 2815) and confirm paras 17-18 (ancillary + before-decision timing), paras 20-21 (exclusive Stridhan outside s.27), and paras 25-29 (CPC s.151 / FCA s.7(1) Expl. (c) route + Devika Joshi treatment). Note: a High Court Full Bench does not bind outside Chhattisgarh; record its jurisdictional weight when citing.

authorities.case: Krishna Kumar Gupta v. Priti Gupta
authorities.claimed_proposition: Return of Stridhan must be determined at trial in a proceeding under the HMA, not independently on a s.27 application; a freestanding s.27 order (Rs. 10,54,364 in lieu of Stridhan, made outside the divorce decree) was set aside. Contrasts s.25, which expressly allows a post-decree application, with s.27, which contains no such language.
authorities.verification_required: Read the full primary judgment (Allahabad HC FA 1116/2024), not the LiveLaw/SCC OnLine news reports, and confirm the holding, the set-aside order, and the s.25 contrast passage. Record whether the judgment is reported with a neutral citation.

authorities.claimed_proposition: Stridhan is the wife's absolute property; the husband (or his family) holding it is a custodian/trustee, so refusal to return it supports criminal breach of trust (now BNS s.316(2), formerly IPC s.406). Used in the graph as the Stridhan authority for hma-27 and bns-316.
authorities.verification_required: Read the full primary judgment ((1985) 2 SCC 370) and confirm: (1) absolute-ownership proposition; (2) custodian/trustee characterisation; (3) that it supports a criminal-breach-of-trust route for withheld Stridhan. The graph itself records this authority as 'lane-supplied, not retest-verified — check against the judgment text before citing in a live answer' (graph v4 unverified_excluded). Do NOT mark verified on the graph's say-so.

authorities.claimed_proposition: PWDVA ss.17/19 shared-household scope: the right to reside in a shared household is not confined to a house owned by the husband; it extends to a house owned by in-laws / joint family where the woman lived in a domestic relationship. Residence / shared-household ONLY — never a custody, guardianship, maintenance or Stridhan precedent.

authorities.claimed_proposition: Maintenance ONLY: quantum criteria for fixing maintenance and the mandatory affidavit of assets and liabilities both parties must file; final directions on overlapping maintenance proceedings (disclose earlier proceedings/orders so the court can adjust). NEVER for Stridhan, custody, residence or divorce.

authorities.claimed_proposition: Family Court retains jurisdiction over Stridhan/property claims even after a divorce decree; an application labelled s.27 must still be adjudicated by the Family Court under FCA s.7(1) Expl. (c) to avoid multiplicity of litigation; a post-decree property order is treated as part of the divorce decree already granted. Does NOT decide a freestanding s.27 application where no HMA proceeding was ever filed.

partially_read.verified_from_read_paras: s.27 application in this case was filed DURING the pendency of the divorce petition (CMA No. 102 of 2017, in HMA Petition No. 140 of 2016; ex parte divorce decree 31 Jan 2018); s.27 'may' is discretionary (para 14); FCA s.7(1) Expl. (c) jurisdiction survives the decree (paras 14, 18); post-decree property order treated as part of the divorce decree (para 20); no opinion on the merits (para 21).
partially_read.warning: The LiveLaw summary phrase 'independent application' means independent of the DECREE (decidable after it), not independent of any proceeding. Anyone citing Astha Thakur for 's.27 needs no proceeding at all' is misreading it. Single High Court decision; does not bind outside Himachal Pradesh; not Supreme Court authority.
